To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the functional body composition of an individual reflects the mass of organs/tissues in a manner that allows the integration of organ/tissue function into the context of metabolic adaptation to disease.
body mass is the product of the number of cells and the mass of each cell, and that cell mass is a product of cell volume and cell density.

the functional body composition is the sum of the individual organ and tissue components, and that it is the relationships between the organ and tissue components that are the determinants of body function and metabolic processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of body composition and function.
the relationships between body components and their functions in the context of weight gain and loss in obesity and cancer‐related cachexia.
understanding the mechanisms of body composition and metabolic adaptation to weight change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Stock Conference has contributed to the development of a new paradigm of body composition research.
body composition is a complex and dynamic process that is regulated by a complex and dynamic system.
the Stock Conferences have contributed to the advancement of body composition and related research and that this has been a fruitful and successful endeavour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concept of functional body composition integrates organ and tissue function and metabolism into body composition.

the concept of functional body composition provides a framework to explain and predict body weight change, body composition and function, and to develop new therapeutic strategies to treat obesity and cachexic cancer patients.

body composition is an important determinant of metabolic health and disease, and that body composition and related metabolic functions should be considered in the development of therapeutic approaches to obesity and cancer cachaxia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
body weight and composition are not just the result of energy intake and expenditure, but rather the result of complex regulatory systems involving crosstalks among organs and tissues.
body composition and function is a highly integrated system that cannot be explained by the study of individual components in isolation.

obesity and cancer cachecia represent extremes of body composition, but the underlying regulatory systems are similar and can be used to understand the changes in body composition that occur in both conditions.
